steps.text: Combine the butter, peanut butter, confectioners' sugar, vanilla and maple flavoring. Cream well and knead well.
Melt the chocolate chips over low heat.
Roll the dough into 1 inch balls. Dip into melted chocolate chips.
Refrigerate overnight (or at least for about 15 minutes) on a cookie sheet lined with wax paper.

raw_recipe.headline: Christmas Peanut Butter Balls
raw_recipe.description: My family makes these Christmas peanut butter balls every year to rave reviews. The maple flavoring is key in making these stand out from other cookies.

video.description: These no-bake, chocolate-covered peanut butter balls have a tasty secret - a hint of maple extract! Bring these crowd-pleasers to your next gathering!

review.reviewBody: I've made these several times and they are always devoured! However, I have never used the maple extract (I just double the vanilla) and prefer milk chocolate over semi-sweet. I think they taste just like Reese Cups.

Great Easy Recipe, made minor changes and included some of the suggestions found here. Doubled the Vanilla no Maple, Used 3 1/4 Cups of Confectioner Sugar, 1/3 cup of butter, 1 3/4 Cups of Luara Scudders Nutty Peanut butter Old Fashion at room temperature and mixed with hand mixer til completely mixed then dumped all out on a cookie sheet and started folding together in to tight balls. It was easy to squeeze mixture in hand and then form into 1" size balls placed on another cookie sheet with wax paper on it and refrigerated all for about an hour. Used toothpick to dip in the heated chocolate used a double boiler then put back in refer. 
Peanut Butter Balls of Perfection. :)
I spoofed the recipe a little and made a peanut butter cookie dough of sorts to be eaten raw. I added 1/8-1/4 cup of water (1/4 cup was a bit too much) and it turned out pretty good.

Awesomely easy = awesomely good. I have been making these for Christmas for several years now. They are always a hit. A few tweaks over the years, 1/2 tsp maple extract and 1/2 tsp corn syrup. Also back off to about 2-1/2 C to 3 C confectioner sugar. Also add 1 tsp of shortening to melted chocolate in double boiler. I roll the balls then pop them in the freezer for about an hour, makes dipping much easier. Love to pipe with melted peanut butter chips for finished look. Tried hiding mini marshmallow in the center of some this year, we'll see how that goes!

I love making these for the holidays or any occasion... it was inspired by a nice woman named Karen. The one thing I use to make my peanut butter balls with the chocolate to hold together is using a product called "gulf wax" right in the canning jar area at ralphs or walmart. I mix it along with the semi-chocolate chips in a double broiler pan on low heat . when it cools off... I dip them and put them back in the fridge to form. Trust me it makes a big difference

I don't keep maple extract, so I used pure maple syrup. Not corn syrup maple "flavored" syrup. I wanted to use crunchy pb, but I did not have enough so I mixed creamy & crunchy. I used the 2 cups of semi-sweet and ran out. So I ended up melting Hershey kisses in double boiler over low heat. I put the pb mix in fridge for a bit to make it easier to handle. I ended up w/ decent looking pieces. I used color sprinkles to "hide" some less than perfect looking areas. Next time I will plan for better chocolate usage. Milk or semi-sweet both work well.

I added only 3 cups of powdered sugar and it still seemed a bit dry after kneading it so I added about 2 T. milk. Also, added 1 t. vanilla extract and 1 T. real maple syrup instead of the maple extract. For the Chocolate I used half milk and half semi-sweet chocolate with a T. of light corn syrup for shine! Next time I will try with 2.5 cups of sugar. Thanks for the base recipe!

I liked them very much and they looked really nice when done. I learned a few things along the way..... at first my dough was too crumbly, I added a half a tablespoon more softened butter and wa la! It was perfect for making into a ball. (it was not to moist either). The next thing I learned was to put the dipped balls onto parchment paper on a plate and into the fridge to harden, as they stuck to the plate without the paper. Lastly I liked the idea of placing each finished and decorated ball into a mini cupcake wrapper. But some of my balls were a bit big, so I learned to make them smaller. They were delish! Very attractive. This round I didn't have maple flavor so used 2 tabs of the vanilla.

Chilling the undipped balls is important prior to coating them. For a failsafe chocolate coating melt 2 T of shortening in a microwave safe bowl. Add chips and stir, mixing well. Microwave 1 minute and stir well. Microwave 30 seconds and stir, and repeat until mixture is smooth.

I always add rice crispies. Also I melt paraffin wax in the chocolate and keep warm while dipping. Hardens quicker and has a nice smooth coating.Additionally I find using a toothpick to dip works best.

Good, but not perfect. If you cut down the confectioners sugar to 3 cups, adding and mixing 1 cup in at a time it makes for the perfect texture and sweetness. Adding a bit of fat to the chocolate also helps with dipping. Try a tbsp of butter, oil or coconut oil. I also make these into peanut butter snowballs quite easily by dipping in icing sugar frosting and tossing in coconut flakes.
Tip would be to hear the peanut butter and butter to make it softer to knead. Also, freeze the calls to make them easier to dip with a toothpick.
The memories! The white chocolate ones are beautiful too but these ones are just like my mom used to make. Sprinkles and all! Great recipe thank you:)
been making these for several years so good
Love the flavor and the texture I add a bit more butter so they are not too dry. We love the great flavor the maple extract adds.
Delicious, make it every year! Thanks mum!
I will make it again and I would use half the maple extract and less sugar and more peanut butter
I made them with 2c PB, 2c sugar, 2t vanilla, milk chocolate chips and 1T shortening. I thought they were still too sweet. I will drop it down to 1c sugar next time.
I loved these!! Instead of 4 cups of sugar I used 2 cups
I loved these!! Instead of 4 cups of sugar I used 2 cups
